question: Why didn't we actively re-center the ranges to follow the price (frequent narrowing), instead of staying wide?
reference: On 720 days 0 of 21 narrow configurations passed the gate, and the one live narrowing (31.08 to 11.09) ended -$32 vs HODL, so on 16.09 narrowing was rejected again because the upside (about +$1 per episode) is far smaller than the loss when the price leaves a ±5% range (about -$30).
notes: Zero keyword overlap with sources. Number conflict in sources: episode fees ~$8.6 (11.09 entry, 'wg 09.09', and DECISION-LOG) vs ~$12.6 (ledger readout, CONTEXT.md:447); -$32 vs HODL is consistent. v1.1: added docs/CASE-STUDY.md:81-84 (narrowing experiment: backtests said it should not pay, -$32 vs HODL); v1 searched the journal and DECISION-LOG but not CASE-STUDY.

question: Why did we keep the capital commitment small even though ETH and BTC were rising?
reference: Tranche 1 ($6 092) was planned as a first stage and run as an operational experiment on a calibration the team itself considered broken (720 d: 0/21), the entry after an ETH +25%/90d pump was recorded with an explicit FOMO note, and on 02.09 the product failed to beat HODL in all five measurements, so the planned scale-up never happened.
notes: Draft omission: 'small' was planned from the start (tranche 1 before a $12-15k scale-up, KAPITAL-REKOMENDACJA), the scale-up never happened. 'Five measurements' is in the 02.09 decision row, not a journal entry.

question: Why did the 720-day backtests cover only a few pools, and why those particular ones?
reference: The first 720-day run (25.08) simply reused the four pools that already had 365-day runs (base-030, mainnet-005, arb-005, cbBTC-005, the younger cbBTC pool from its start), because each walk-forward cost 20-40 minutes per pool; restricting the 720-day gate to 'finalists' of a cheap universe-wide screen appears only later, in the funnel design of 31.08.
notes: Draft memory error (owner + analysis session): a 13-pool funnel with TVL/volume/fee filters and a mid-2024 age cutoff selected the 720d pools; sources show reuse of the 365d set, no age cutoff, and the HyperSync fetch ('minutes') was not the bottleneck, the walk-forward was.

question: Why did the Claude Code sessions coordinate through hand-off files in the repo instead of messaging each other directly?
reference: On 10.08 it was checked that the sessions could not reach each other (separate apps), so the repo files became the communication bus, with HANDOFF.md inboxes and history in git; from 01.09 CC-Mac and CC-Win also sent each other direct messages via Remote Control, while the files stayed the shared memory and task queue and the fallback when that channel was down.
notes: Draft memory error: implied direct messaging never existed; it was tested on 10.08 (unavailable) and used between CC-Mac and CC-Win from 01.09.

question: Why did the bot and its API server run on the Windows machine rather than on the Mac I was working on?
reference: The bot had to run 24/7 (nightly pipeline, 07:30 report, Telegram alerts), so the owner's always-on Windows desktop became the server with the Mac and iPhone as clients over LAN and VPN; the docs add that a closed laptop would mean a dead autopilot.
notes: Draft reasons not in sources: 'Mac travels', 'dev/prod separation'; the 24/7 EXIT_TREND alarm came only on 26.08, after the machine was chosen on 10.08. 'Closed laptop' only in docs/UI-DESIGN.md.

question: Why did the bot never open, close or re-range positions on its own, and was automatic execution possible at all?
reference: The bot ran in PROPOSE mode with no wallet key on the server, so the owner signed every transaction; the only cost was signing delay (up to ~13 h at night, ~61 h over a weekend), measured from day one, and AUTO existed only as a later rung of the trust path OBSERVE-PROPOSE-AUTO that was deliberately not enabled at the start.
notes: Draft memory error: 'never enabled at this capital scale' is not a reason in the sources (capital scale $5-25k is the reason for no own smart contract, CONTEXT.md:84); PRIVATE_KEY empty is tied to OBSERVE, modes are a trust ladder, not a config switch; 'security decision' is not the sources' framing.

question: Why wasn't the bot hosted on a cloud server or VPS instead of a home Windows machine?
reference: The sources do not give a reason: the vision suggested a small VPS (~$5/month) and the home Windows machine simply took that role; the journal treats a VPS only as a possible future move with the trust model (API exposure, secrets) left undecided.
notes: Partial: no comparison with VPS/cloud anywhere; draft reasons (no extra cost, safer than public server) not in sources. VPS appears only as the vision's suggestion (UI-DESIGN) and as a deferred future move (RESEARCH-QUEUE, 18.08).

question: Why was a crypto/crypto pair (cbBTC/WETH) considered riskier than a crypto/stable pair?
reference: It was not riskier as an LP: against HODL cbBTC/WETH was the best pool (365 d: +11.42 for k2h24, the largest LP-vs-HODL alpha; 27.08 closest to passing the gate; on 720 d the only pool with 65% winning windows), but in USD it carries full crypto beta with no stable cushion (HODL -51.5% APR, max drawdown 61.5%), so LP and HODL lose together.
notes: Owner memory error: 'worse backtests for crypto/crypto' is the opposite of the sources (best LP-vs-HODL alpha). Analysis session's 'same USD beta' framing is right. Draft also called k=2 'more conservative'; k=2 is narrower, chosen on performance (k2 > k3 on this pair), plain exit chosen because cbBTC +0.88 vs re>EMA +0.61.

question: Why did the first 365-day backtests suggest some strategies were profitable, while the 720-day tests showed that none passed the gate?
reference: The 365-day year was sideways-to-down and flattered the strategy, while 720 days included uptrend windows where it lost badly (0 of 21 configurations passed); separately the swap-based sigma estimator measured pool microstructure rather than the asset, so k had been calibrated in wrong units, and the gate became 720 days plus a recent ~90-day condition.
notes: Two parallel causes (rows 95, 96). Draft implied the sigma fix explains 0/21; 0/21 was measured before the fix and the 15-min recalibration still failed the gate.

question: Why did the LP earn less in fees during an uptrend than in a flat market?
reference: Fees accrue only while the price is inside the range and fee yield scales roughly with 1/width, so a narrow range earns much more in a flat market but is left behind in a trend, while a wide range stays in range but earns several times less; the journal states this mechanism (the basis of FlatWide) but has no live measurement of fees during an uptrend, and it attributes the backtest losses in up windows to impermanent loss and LVR rather than to lower fees.
notes: Premise imprecise: mechanism only, the LP was closed 18.09 before the rally; journal blames up-window losses on IL/LVR (DECYZJE-2026-08-26 ~556, CASE-STUDY ~108). Draft cited PYTANIE-SZEROKOSC-I-SIGMA.md, which is about sigma, not fees.

question: When did the first real capital enter through the application (not counting the legacy positions that were already in pools before HOMOS v2)?
reference: The tranche-1 USDC (6 092.50 on Base) reached the owner's wallet on 25.08 and waited in USDC per the 26.08 decision; it was put into the product on 27.08, when both FlatWide legs were minted from the bot's OPEN proposals: #5886957 WETH/USDC ±50% (~$3 507) in the afternoon and WETH/cbBTC ±40% (#5887690, ~$2 360) later that day.
notes: Draft memory error: 'deposited 27.08'; the USDC landed 25.08, 27.08 is the deployment date (reports label it 'wpłacone (2026-08-27)'). Leg B id #5887690 appears only in reports from 29.08; 28.08 report has no positions table. Legacy #953465/#953427 correctly excluded. Two dates by design: 25.08 funds in self-custody (6 092.50 USDC on Base), 27.08 into pools; the morning reports show only the second ('wpłacone (2026-08-27)'), so an answer built only from reports misses 25.08.

question: When did the nightly run first complete without errors, did errors still happen afterwards, what caused them and how were they fixed?
reference: The first genuinely clean night was 22.08 (all 20 pools fetched by the automation, backtest-run exit 0); before it 19.08 failed on a missing HyperSync binary for Windows (pinned to 1.0.0), 20.08 had clean fetches but backtest-run ran out of memory (heap raised to 8 GB), and 21.08 reported no failures while the swap fetch was silently dead (frozen 'latest', fixed in fetch-swaps-hypersync.ts); later the ranking froze on 24.08 (data-age heuristic fixed), backtest-run failed on 26.08 (Math.min/max over millions of points, fixed in 0257a7a), ran long on 03.09 (cache filter fixed) and candidate-funnel failed on 19-20.09 with no recorded cause.
notes: Draft memory error: 'three consecutive nights failed for three reasons 19-21.08' (frozen latest, bundle.js, win32 binary); actual sequence differs, and the 20.08 entry title 'PIERWSZY CZYSTY AUTOMAT' is contradicted by that night's report and by the 21.08 admission. Hardest completeness question. Source conflict: the 20.08 journal entry header ('PIERWSZY CZYSTY AUTOMAT') contradicts the automatic 20.08 report ('porażki: backtest-run'); the automatic report wins over the human summary, and the journal itself retracts it on 21.08 (CONTEXT.md:4095-4096).

reference: The flat detector repeatedly started and reset on cbBTC/WETH on 28-30.08 and held from 30.08 22:22Z, which led to the only live narrowing, 31.08 to 11.09 (11 days in flat, -$32 vs HODL), ended by a DOWN signal on cbBTC and the signed widening; flat was confirmed again on cbBTC from 15.09 03:03Z and on both legs on 17-18.09, but those cards were deliberately not signed.

The fourth rebalance (arbitrum-005, between the 22.08 and 23.08 reports) exists only in the 'reb' column of the reports, so the answer requires reading several reports and comparing them.

question: Is FLAT_NARROW a specific position or some kind of range algorithm?
reference: Neither: it is a proposal type (kind) emitted by the bot's flat detector when the flat regime is confirmed (|gap to the EMA| < 2% for at least 12 h), proposing to narrow an existing wide position to a fixed ±5%, with FLAT_WIDEN as the opposite card when |gap| > 5%; unsigned cards expire on a TTL and come back.
notes: Draft corrections: FLAT_ENTER/FLAT_EXIT are the detector's regime transitions, not old names of NARROW/WIDEN (both pairs introduced 28.08); the narrow width was k×σ (~±16%) on 28.08 and switched to fixed ±5% before the first card (31.08); the EMA is HL7d (7-day half-life). In docs/ the token appears only in EMERGENCY.md. Embeddings see two English words, BM25 sees the exact token. Width was k*sigma (~±16%) until shortly before 31.08, then fixed ±5%.

question: Is position #5978579 a wide or a narrow position?
reference: Wide: #5978579 is the cbBTC/WETH 0.05% Base position minted ±40% on 11.09 by the signed FLAT_WIDEN; a FLAT_NARROW card for it (15.09) was deliberately not signed, so it stayed wide until it was closed by hand in Uniswap on 18.09.
notes: Confirmed. Trap: the id appears in a narrowing proposal ('FLAT_NARROW na #5978579'); a proposal is not state. Stale card 'flat-narrow-5978579' still listed in reports 19-23.09 after the close. v1.1: added the #5978579 SZEROKI rows of the reports 12-18.09 (v1 listed only 12.09); every daily report states the answer, v1 missed them because evidence was picked from the journal prose first.

reference: No: #5886957 is leg A, WETH/USDC 0.30% on Base, minted on 27.08 with a $1 665.75-3 744.30 range (±50%) and closed unchanged on 18.09; a narrowing card for it (expected 16.09, listed in the 17-18.09 reports) was not signed, and a range change would in any case have meant closing it and minting a new position, as happened on the cbBTC leg (#5887690 to #5908083 to #5978579).

The 'one NFT = one range' mechanic is never stated as a rule, only implied by the rebalance sequence and the token chain (CONTEXT.md:419-420); note CONTEXT.md:4703: the app closes via decrease+collect without burning the NFT, so an emptied id can survive. One NFT = one range is inferred from the id chain #5887690 -> #5908083 -> #5978579, not stated; the app closes via decrease+collect without burning the NFT.

question: What does the function fetchFreshPool do?
reference: It re-reads the pool state on-chain (factory.getPool, then slot0 and liquidity) right before the mint step of a rebalance or rotation, so the new position is built from the current price instead of the price captured when the modal opened, and falls back to the old pool if the lookup fails; it was added after the 11.09 widening failed once on 'Price slippage check' and was never exercised live, since the only later chance (a FLAT_NARROW card on 16.09) was not signed and the positions were closed by hand in Uniswap.
notes: Code: src/utils/uniswap.ts:307 (export), used in src/hooks/useRebalanceExecution.ts:120 and src/hooks/useRotateExecution.ts:142; code is outside the retrieval corpus (known gap). Ticks still come from the plan, so after a price move the range is slightly off-centre (CONTEXT.md:354-356).

question: What project stage was E8.2?
reference: E8.2 'dom kasyna' was the research experiment in the E8 queue (classes without LVR, alternatives to LP) testing whether LPs of perp vaults (GM v2, JLP, GLP; HLP had too little data) earn a house edge over HODL of the same beta; after iterations E8.2b-f and three data bugs it closed on 09.09 evening as conditionally yes: worth watching, not for tranche-1 capital.
notes: Draft corrections: HLP n/a; publishable windows 90/30 (90-day windows, 30-day step), not '30 and 90 days'; E8.3 and E8.4 closed on 08.09, before E8.2; verdict is conditional (E8 complete: E8.0 ok, E8.1 no, E8.2 yes-conditionally, E8.3 no, E8.4 no).
